accroche: Onstage before 80,000 people, the chorus starts looping endlessly: “Girl you know it's, girl you know it's…”
contenu_vulgarise:
In 1989, the duo Milli Vanilli, formed by dancers Rob Pilatus and Fab Morvan, enjoys a meteoric success: their hit *Girl You Know It's True* stays twenty-six weeks on the Billboard Hot 100. They join the Club MTV tour, alongside Paula Abdul and Tone Loc, to give their first big concerts.

During a stop before eighty thousand spectators at Lake Compounce park, in Bristol, Connecticut, the incident happens during the chorus. The recorded track starts looping: “Girl you know it's, girl you know it's, girl you know it's…,” the word “true” never coming. Pilatus would later tell the *Los Angeles Times*: “I knew right then and there, it was the beginning of the end for Milli Vanilli. When my voice got stuck in the computer and it just kept repeating and repeating, I panicked. I just ran off the stage.”

## What the incident reveals, belatedly

Despite this incident, widely noticed but not yet read as a confession, the duo keeps piling up awards: three trophies at the American Music Awards in January 1990, then the Grammy for Best New Artist in February, beating the Indigo Girls and Tone Loc.

The truth, revealed by producer Frank Farian himself in November 1990, goes beyond mere stage lip-syncing: Pilatus and Morvan sang not a single note, neither in concert nor on the album. The voices heard on it are those of several singers recruited separately by Farian, including Brad Howell, John Davis, and Charles Shaw, blended in the studio. Pilatus and Morvan, spotted in Munich, where they lived in public housing and stole food to survive, had been hired solely as the group's faces, for four thousand dollars each. Farian had already done something similar in the 1970s with his group Boney M., whose dancer Bobby Farrell did not sing on the records, without causing a scandal.

## What it shifts

On November 19, 1990, the American Academy of Recording Arts takes the Grammy for Best New Artist away from Milli Vanilli, a first in the award's history. Lip-syncing onstage was, at the time, an already widespread practice and rarely punished. What caused the scandal was therefore not lip-syncing itself, but its discovery: a similar gesture, which had caused no scandal with Boney M., becomes a worldwide affair the moment the public has proof of it, in the form of a chorus that will not stop looping.

carte.punch: Before 80,000 people, the chorus starts looping endlessly: the lip-syncing has just given itself away.
carte.idee: In 1989, Milli Vanilli's tape gets stuck in the middle of a concert, repeating the same bit of a phrase. The duo nonetheless keeps collecting awards, up to the 1990 Grammy. A year later, the producer confesses: they never sang a single note.

pour_aller_plus_loin.note: The full story, from the spotting of the two dancers in Munich to the withdrawal of the Grammy.

quiz.question: What, precisely, set off the scandal around Milli Vanilli in November 1990?
choix: The publication of an investigative article by a journalist who had infiltrated the recording studio
The admission of producer Frank Farian himself, revealing that the duo had never sung a single note
A lawsuit brought by the real singers demanding to be credited on the album
The discovery of a contract signed by Pilatus and Morvan admitting their inability to sing
quiz.explication: The 1989 Bristol concert incident had already planted a doubt, but it is indeed the admission of producer Frank Farian himself, in November 1990, that sets off the scandal and leads to the withdrawal of the Grammy a few days later. No investigative article, lawsuit, or publicized contract figures in the chain of events.

choix: At Madison Square Garden in New York, before 20,000 spectators
At a festival in Los Angeles, before 50,000 spectators
During a live television broadcast, before millions of viewers
At Lake Compounce park, in Bristol, Connecticut, before 80,000 spectators
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The incident takes place at a concert before eighty thousand spectators at Lake Compounce park, in Bristol, Connecticut.

quiz_supplementaire.question: Whose voices are really heard on Milli Vanilli's recordings?
choix: Rob Pilatus and Fab Morvan themselves, but electronically reworked in the studio
Several singers recruited separately by Frank Farian, including Brad Howell, John Davis, and Charles Shaw
Members of the group Boney M, reusing their old recordings from the 1970s
Anonymous backing singers whose identity was never revealed, even after the scandal
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The voices heard are those of several singers recruited separately by producer Frank Farian, including Brad Howell, John Davis, and Charles Shaw, blended in the studio.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What distinguishes the Milli Vanilli case from Frank Farian's practice with Boney M. in the 1970s?
choix: Boney M.'s lip-syncing concerned only tours, never studio albums
Boney M. never used studio voices, unlike Milli Vanilli
The method used with Boney M. had caused no scandal, whereas Milli Vanilli's method burst into the open
Farian never used this method before Milli Vanilli, contrary to what is believed
quiz_supplementaire.explication: Farian had already done something similar with Boney M. in the 1970s, where the dancer Bobby Farrell did not sing on the records, without causing a scandal, before Milli Vanilli's method burst into the open in 1990.
